fema_nfhl.name: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, as the observatory's flood layer (flood.geojson)
fema_nfhl.license: US Government work; FEMA's metadata lists no access constraints

noaa_slr.name: NOAA Office for Coastal Management, Sea Level Rise Viewer data for Puerto Rico (3 ft above mean higher high water, connected to the ocean)
noaa_slr.license: No license stated; NOAA's disclaimer applies

usgs_landslide_map.name: USGS landslide susceptibility map of Puerto Rico (Hughes and Schulz, 2020; GIS layer, 2021), read from the first author's tile copy as landslide.py does
usgs_landslide_map.license: US federal government data (public domain); the data release states CC0 1.0

fx_layers.name: PR Data Observatory facility layers (USGS, OpenStreetMap, HUD, EIA, FAA), the NCES school directory through the Urban Institute's Education Data API, and FHWA HPMS main roads
fx_layers.license: Each layer keeps its source's terms: US federal sources (USGS, HUD, EIA, FAA, NCES, FHWA); police stations and city halls are OpenStreetMap (ODbL); the Education Data API asks for credit (ODC-By)

notes.kind: overlaid: one published layer laid on another (HANDOFF decision 107)
notes.flood_area: FEMA's 1% annual chance flood area (Special Flood Hazard Area), from the observatory's simplified flood layer
notes.sea_level_rise: NOAA's extent of 3 ft of sea level rise above mean higher high water, connected to the ocean; low-lying areas not connected are left out
notes.landslide: the USGS susceptibility classes High, Very High and Extremely High under each point (zoom-15 tiles, about 4.5 m); roads read every 20 m; Vieques and Culebra are not in the map
notes.left_out: bridges (over water by design), public housing developments whose location is approximate, and points that share their coordinates with another point of the same layer (several facilities listed at one address)
notes.overlap: library points within 150 m of an open public school may be the same building; both are counted
notes.drawn: the public schools as a map layer (public_schools.geojson) and the hazard flags of every facility point in its pop-up (facility_hazards.json)
